headline: Adopted Site Plan Regulation changes on parking and driveways; approved the Hoit Road lot line adjustment and a Sanders Street driveway permit; postponed several projects.
summary: Adopted changes to site plan rules on parking, driveways, loading, and lighting, effective when City Council adopts related zoning changes. Approved a lot line adjustment at 109 Hoit Road and a driveway permit on a Sanders Street parcel. Continued several projects, including 270 Loudon Road and 94-98 Manchester Street, to a later date.

Mr. Thompson stated staff is recommending the Board approve the proposed amendments to the Site 
Plan Regulations, to be effective upon the City Council adopting related Zoning Ordinance 
Amendments, which are scheduled for public hearing on October 13.  This amendment effort follows 
a robust review of regulatory requirements surrounding parking (including at least a dozen drafts and 
iterations of proposed regulatory changes), and a collaborative process with many Community 
Development Department staff members.  Through this effort, staff has coalesced around the proposal 
now being presented to the Planning Board, focusing on mechanisms for relief from the regulatory 
standards as an interim step, understanding that wholesale policy changes are best suited for 
development following the completion of the Master Plan process, which is now underway.   If 
adopted, these amendments will provide significantly increased flexibility for relief from the 
regulatory requirements associated with parking, loading, and driveway access.  The shift of the 
majority of design standards to the Site Plan Regulations allows the use of waivers, a less stringent 
statutory standard of relief, administered by the Planning Board, eliminating most of the need to seek 
variance relief from the Zoning Board of Adjustment.  For the minority of projects that do not require 
site plan review, the related Zoning Ordinance amendments will create conditional use permit relief 
valves, again putting administration of relief in the hands of the Planning Board rather than the 
ZBA.  Lastly, these regulation amendments (in conjunction with the related Zoning amendments) 
eliminate the challenges associated with differing standards that exist today between the regulations 
and Zoning Ordinance. 
 
Chair Woodfin opened the public hearing, after receiving no public testimony, Chair Woodfin closed 
the public hearing.  
 
On a motion made by Chair Woodfin, seconded by Member Rosenberger, the Board voted 7-0-0 to 
adopt the proposed Site Plan Regulation Amendments to Sections 18, 19, 20, and 29, effective upon 
the City Council's adoption of the related zoning ordinance amendments.

energy grid demands and electricity costs for Concord residents.
Water and Environmental Pressures: While the project claims to use single-

demands and potential impacts on nearby wetland buffers. 
Incompatibility with the Area: Locke Road and East Concord are not
appropriate zones for high-density AI and server infrastructure, which offer very
few permanent, local jobs while shifting long-term environmental and
infrastructure risks onto taxpayers.

cumulative impacts on New Hampshire's power grid.
